root.name: Center Game: l'Hermet Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. Qxd4 Nc6 4. Qe3 f5

overview: After 4.Qe3 Black attacks e4 at once with 4...f5 rather than the usual 4...Nf6. White can answer 5.Nc3 or 5.exf5, and Black's king is loosened on the e8-h5 diagonal and the e-file while White's queen is already placed in the centre. White generally gets the easier development; Black hopes to use the extra tempo from attacking the queen's pawn support. I am not certain of the details.

white_ideas.idea: Nc3 and Bd3 to pile on e4 and the weakened e8-h5 diagonal
exf5 and Qe3 pressure on the e-file against the Black king

black_ideas.idea: Keep the f5 pawn and develop with ...Nf6 and ...Bb4
Hit the white queen with ...Bb4 and ...Nf6 for tempo

typical_structures.structure: Open centre, White queen on e3, Black pawns on f5 and d7

character.notes: Black's ...f5 opens the king and the e-file, so tactics decide.

gambit.notes: The d4 pawn was exchanged and material is level; ...f5 offers no pawn that White can safely keep.

soundness.notes: The pawn move weakens the king for little; White probably stands better.

structure.notes: Open e-file and diagonals with pieces active.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom meet the Paulsen with ...f5.

level.notes: A rare sideline with thin theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Paulsen 4...Nf6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. Qxd4 Nc6 4. Qe3 Nf6

character.reason: An early ...f5 opens the king and the e-file, so tactics decide quickly.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn has been sacrificed.

soundness.reason: The pawn move weakens Black's king for little and White probably stands better.

structure.reason: The e-file and diagonals are open and pieces play on them.

approach.reason: Strong players rarely choose 4...f5 in the Center Game.

level.reason: Little theory and modest plans, but not a coach's first choice.

plans.reason: White's queen is already central and has to avoid tempo-losing attacks.
